findings.claim: The verify section initialises `FAIL=0` at line 343, unconditionally overwriting the `FAIL=1` set by the apply-phase failure handlers at lines 322 and 329. When an apply call fails (`APPLY_FAIL=1`) but the subsequent verification passes because the pre-existing branch state already matched the desired posture, the script exits 0 and emits `verification passed ✓` despite a failed API call. The code comment at line 308 ("then exiting non-zero") and the bootstrap-only header invariant added in fix-round-2 COMP-R2-005 ("emits a log block on EVERY completed invocation... then exiting non-zero") are both violated for this case.
findings.evidence: Line 312: `APPLY_FAIL=0`. Line 317: `|| APPLY_FAIL=1` captures PUT failure. Line 322: `FAIL=1` propagates PUT failure. Line 325: `|| APPLY_FAIL=1` captures POST failure. Line 329: `FAIL=1` propagates POST failure. Line 343: `FAIL=0` — unconditional reset clobbers both prior FAIL=1 assignments. Lines 344-347: verify checks accumulate a fresh FAIL=1 only if the current state is wrong. Lines 353-367: `if [ "${FAIL:-0}" -ne 0 ]` reads only the verify-phase FAIL. Line 435: `if [ "${FAIL:-0}" -ne 0 ]; then exit 1; fi` exits 0 when verify passed. Concrete trigger: PUT fails with 403 on a repo whose branch protection is already in the desired state (idempotent re-run) — verify sees the correct state, FAIL stays 0, exit 0, 'verification passed ✓' emitted. Alternatively: POST /required_signatures fails transiently but signatures were already enabled by a prior 020J run — same outcome. In both cases the stderr ERROR message and the 'verification passed ✓' stdout message directly contradict each other.
findings.impact: Any scripted caller checking the exit code receives a false-success signal when an API call failed. The contradiction between the ERROR stderr message and the stdout 'verification passed ✓' line degrades operator trust in the log output. The documented invariant 'then exiting non-zero' is broken. The audit trail records the ERROR message so the failure is not fully silent, but the exit-code contract is violated.
findings.mitigation: Accumulate the apply-phase failure independently of the verify-phase FAIL. Minimal one-line fix: replace `FAIL=0` at line 343 with `FAIL=${APPLY_FAIL:-0}` so the verify-phase OR-accumulates on top of any apply-phase failure. Then the final `if [ "${FAIL:-0}" -ne 0 ]; then exit 1; fi` at line 435 correctly exits non-zero on any failure in either phase. Alternative: rename the verify accumulator to `VERIFY_FAIL` (initialised to 0) and change the final exit to `if [ "${APPLY_FAIL:-0}" -ne 0 ] || [ "${VERIFY_FAIL:-0}" -ne 0 ]; then exit 1; fi`.

findings.claim: The `AFTER_JSON` GET at line 336 is unprotected under `set -e`. Fix-round-2 closure COMP-R2-005 added the guarantee 'the script emits a log block on EVERY completed invocation, including verification failures and partial-state apply failures' to the bootstrap-only header. A transient GET failure at line 336 causes `set -e` to abort before the log block at line 397, violating the guarantee just strengthened in this same fix round.
findings.evidence: Line 336: `AFTER_JSON="$(gh api -X GET "repos/${REPO}/branches/${BRANCH}/protection")"` — no `|| fallback`, no error accumulator. Contrast lines 276-287 (BEFORE_RAW capture) which uses `|| BEFORE_STATUS=$?` and then branches on the error pattern. The bootstrap-only header language 'EVERY completed invocation' was added in COMP-R2-005 (FIX-ROUND-2.md line 42); the unprotected GET predates fix-round-2 but the documentation promise is new, creating a fresh document-code mismatch introduced in this fix round.
findings.impact: A transient GET failure during verify (network hiccup, rate limit) after a successful PUT would leave the apply unlogged. The operator's audit trail has no record that branch protection was changed. Low probability but non-zero, especially in rate-limited enterprise environments.
findings.mitigation: Mirror the BEFORE_RAW pattern: `AFTER_JSON="$(gh api -X GET "repos/${REPO}/branches/${BRANCH}/protection" 2>&1)" || { echo 'WARNING: verify GET failed; cannot confirm state' >&2; FAIL=1; AFTER_JSON='{"_note":"GET failed — see stderr"}'; }`. This ensures the log block always emits and records the failure context.

probes_verified.probe_1_apply_fail_set_e: PASS — `printf '%s' "$PAYLOAD" | gh api ... >/dev/null || APPLY_FAIL=1` is a compound list under `||`. POSIX and bash both exempt the left side of `||` from `set -e` abort; if the pipeline exits non-zero, `APPLY_FAIL=1` is evaluated, not an exit. The `pipefail` option affects which pipeline stage's exit code is used but does not change the `||` exception. Assignment is always reached on failure.
probes_verified.probe_2_traversal_false_positive: PASS — `*..*` matches strings containing the literal two-character sequence `..`. `actions.github.io/contributions` contains three isolated single dots but no adjacent pair; the substring `..` is absent. None of the four case arms (`*..*`, `.*`, `*/.*`, `*/..*`) fire. The string then satisfies `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`. No false-positive.

GitHub branch-protection API returns immediately-consistent state for this sub-resource. The `sigs_enabled` check at line 153 reads `.required_signatures.enabled` which is `true` after the POST regardless of prior 020J state. Verify holds.
probes_verified.probe_4_payload_scope: PASS — `PAYLOAD` assigned at line 293 via `build_payload`. No unset between line 293 and the `cat <<EOF` log block at line 397. `printf '%s' "$PAYLOAD"` at line 414 (inside the heredoc) is in scope.
probes_verified.probe_5_conditional_verification_passed: PARTIAL FAIL — the else-branch placement relative to the verify checks is correct: `if [ "${FAIL:-0}" -ne 0 ]` at line 353 comes after the four checks at lines 344-347 that accumulate `FAIL=1`. But `FAIL=0` at line 343 resets apply-phase `FAIL=1` before those checks run. When an apply call failed but verify passes, the else-branch emits 'verification passed ✓' in contradiction of the apply error. This is CORR3-001.
probes_verified.probe_6_ack_flag_before_mutation: PASS — ack-flag-without-trigger guard at lines 181-185 fires during argument validation before the first API call (line 316). Exit 2 with no API mutation.

CORR2-001.evidence: Lines 353-367: `if [ "${FAIL:-0}" -ne 0 ]` gates the failure path; `log "verification passed ✓"` emits only in the else-branch. The unconditional emission is eliminated. Placement is correct: the if/else block follows the four verify checks that accumulate FAIL=1 at lines 344-347.

CORR2-002.evidence: Lines 213-217: case-statement `*..*|.*|*/.*|*/..*` precedes the regex. `owner/..` is caught by the `*/..*` arm (owner matches `*`, then literal `/..`, then `*` matches empty). `actions.github.io/contributions` contains only isolated dots — the two-character sequence `..` is absent — so no case arm fires and the string proceeds to the regex, where it matches `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`. No false-positive on legitimate dotted names.

CORR2-003.evidence: Lines 181-185: `if [ "$ACK_ADMIN_BYPASS" -eq 1 ] && [ "$ENFORCE_ADMINS" = "true" ]` emits an explicit error and exits 2. This fires during argument validation (line 181), before the first API call at line 316. No partial state is possible.

CORR2-004.evidence: configure-020d2-required-check.sh lines 81-105: unified PUT heredoc contains no `required_signatures` field (grep confirms no occurrence in the JSON body). Separate `gh api -X POST .../protection/required_signatures` added at line 117. Verification block reads `.required_signatures.enabled` via GET at line 131 after the POST completes synchronously — check holds.

structured_review.summary: All four R2 correctness findings are closed. Fix-round-2 introduces one MIN regression (CORR3-001): the `FAIL=0` reset at line 343 discards the apply-phase `FAIL=1` set at lines 322/329, causing the script to exit 0 with 'verification passed ✓' when an API call failed but the pre-existing state already satisfied the desired posture — violating the documented 'then exiting non-zero' contract. One nit (CORR3-002): the AFTER_JSON GET at line 336 is unprotected under `set -e`, creating a fresh document-code gap with the log-emission guarantee strengthened in COMP-R2-005. CORR3-001 requires a one-line fix (`FAIL=${APPLY_FAIL:-0}` in place of `FAIL=0` at line 343) before this slice reaches correctness fixpoint. CORR3-002 is advisory.
